A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TiRex and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Existing material can be matched reliably across the additions and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original forecasting evaluations, component ablations, sensitivity analyses, inference measurements, and fine-tuning results.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds a multivariate-subset analysis and TiRex 1.1 evaluation.

M1.justification: Appendix E introduces long-period normalization for TiRex 1.1: identify the dominant frequency and resample so one period fits the context. This extends preprocessing while retaining the original xLSTM architecture, CPM, quantile loss, and augmentations.

E1.justification: TiRex 1.1 substantially revises training coverage: all GiftEval datasets are excluded across sampling frequencies, a potentially overlapping Alabama solar subset is removed, and Chronos-ZS datasets outside GiftEval are added. The evaluation benchmark collections remain unchanged; the multivariate analysis reuses existing GiftEval data.

E2.justification: The added full-GiftEval comparison in Figure 19 includes Toto Base 1.0, Sundial Base, and YingLong 300m alongside retained comparators. Existing comparisons remain intact; COSMIC is added only to related work.

E3.justification: Appendix E adds evaluation of TiRex 1.1 with full-GiftEval training exclusion and long-period resampling; Appendix D.3 adds multivariate-subset aggregation. Original evaluation settings remain unchanged. The seasonal-naive update is disclosed as context, without switching the reported scores to the updated computation.

E4.justification: New Appendix D.3 and Figure 14 isolate multivariate datasets to examine whether independently forecasting each variate remains competitive with multivariate models. Existing component ablations, sensitivity analyses, fine-tuning analysis, and qualitative examples are retained.

E5.justification: The original six-seed standard deviations, Table 1's three-standard-deviation comparison criterion, and 24 fine-tuning runs are retained. No additional statistical procedure or increased run count is specified for TiRex 1.1.

E6.justification: Figure 19 adds a benchmark-wide TiRex 1.1 comparison, reporting full-GiftEval CRPS 0.41, MASE 0.64, and average CRPS rank 3.0, plus newer competitors' results. Figure 14 adds multivariate-subset scores of 0.40 and 0.61, with rank 3.1. Original results remain intact; TiRex 1.1 uses different training and preprocessing conditions, so its scores do not establish a controlled performance gain.

T1.justification: The forecasting definitions, losses, sLSTM equations, data-generation formulas, and expressivity diagram are unchanged. The added expressivity explanation is a hypothesis, without a new theorem, derivation, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about TiRex, CPM, augmentations, and strong short- and long-horizon zero-shot forecasting. The appendix additions provide further supporting evidence without redefining these main claims.

C2.justification: v2 newly acknowledges uncertain cross-frequency solar overlap and qualifies the interpretation of absolute scores following a seasonal-naive baseline update. It also explains spike randomization as encouraging generalization to transient events and adds representation reuse for classification or anomaly detection as future work.

D1.justification: Appendix E documents TiRex 1.1's corpus-filtering rules and outlines frequency-based resampling; Section 4 and Appendix C.3 identify the historical leaderboard computation used. Original hyperparameters, hardware information, and code access remain unchanged, while implementation details for the new preprocessing remain brief.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for COSMIC, Toto, Sundial, Yinglong, forecasting-model feature extraction, and the dedicated TabPFN-TS work. These update the surrounding literature and concurrent comparisons without substantially changing the paper's research positioning.

P1.justification: Localized explanations, qualifications, acknowledgments, and conference identification are updated. Two appendix sections are added with corresponding renumbering, while the main narrative and section organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figures 14 and 19 for the multivariate subset and TiRex 1.1 comparisons. All 19 original figures are retained, with some renumbering and relocation; tables retain their structures, and other layout and caption edits are limited.

improvement.justification: Appendix E strengthens full-GiftEval validation through more conservative training-data exclusions, including the uncertain solar overlap. Newer competitors, the multivariate breakdown, and score-computation disclosure improve evidential coverage and transparency. These gains are limited by the brief preprocessing description and absence of uncertainty reporting for TiRex 1.1's new scores.
